title: Armstrong has him dance Lady Be Good
summary: Armstrong, who started calling him son, liked to watch Green dance Lady Be Good while Chuckles played vibraphone, and had them repeat it as an encore.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Yes, he was a great personality.
And I understand you got very close to him.
Yes, got so close he started to calling me son.
Well, I'm very interested in the kind of relationship you formed, and how he responded to tap dancers and how he incorporated that in his own act.

Well, he insisted on us doing a dance. He liked to see me dance like John Bubbles at that time, because John Bubbles was known as a great jazz singer. And he liked to see me dance -- tap dance -- 'Lady Be Good', you see. As I say, it was more like a band leader dancing, you see. It was something in the dance that he enjoyed. I guess it was the circling, I think it was. It reminded him of his trumpet, you see.
Well, what kind of dancing did you do with him? Can you explain some of it -- and I'd also like to see it.

Well, I call it syncopated tap, you see, and of course it was up tempo, very fast, you know. It was a jolly, a merry tempo in tap dancing, you see. Chuckles would be playing his solo on the vibraphones and Chuckles has acquired a new style of comedy. He would operatic singing -- scat singing but he would do it operatically, you see, like some opera star, you know. And he was actually singing operatic, but he'd be scatting, you see, which I couldn't do (unintelligible) a lot of range, you know. But the tap dancing would happen like right after he'd play the introduction -- he played the introduction -- eight-bar introduction, then he'd go into the melody of "Lady Be Good." So, he would play like a chorus and I would tap dance a chorus and come back around like and lead the band for the next half of a chorus going out. That's what Satchmo enjoyed. In case sometime we would have to do an encore, he would make us repeat this number, "Lady Be Good," so he could see the tap dance again, you see. That's what we did.
Can you show me what it was like?
Well, I can show you the tap step that he liked in the tap dance. Would that be all right?
Is there something you'd like to say, Chuck, about the dance you just did?
Yes. Well, it became a favorite of Louis
